name: San Francisco Proposition I (November 1994)
effective: Date of certification, for covered units (the certification date is not stated in the text)

components.cap_unit: percent of the rise in the regional consumer price index
source_sentences: Rental units in owner-occupied buildings of two to four units built before June 1979 become subject to the Rent Ordinance.
For a covered unit, the landlord may raise the rent of a sitting tenant once a year by no more than the allowable increase, which is 60 percent of the rise in the regional consumer price index.
When a tenant leaves voluntarily, the landlord may set the rent for the next tenant freely, after which the limit applies again.
Rental units in owner-occupied buildings of two to four units built before June 1979 become subject to the Rent Ordinance.
Tenants of covered units may be evicted only for one of the just causes listed in the Rent Ordinance.

unclear.text: The Rent Board hears tenant petitions and landlord applications and may order rent reductions and refunds.
readings: U1-a: The Rent Board's power to order reductions and refunds enforces the rent limit in C1 and adds no separate restriction.
U1-b: The Rent Board's power is a separate operative provision on rent adjudication, which no listed instrument covers.

context: Since 1979 the San Francisco Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance has limited annual rent increases for sitting tenants in most rental buildings built before June 1979. (policy.txt, line 5)
Buildings of four units or fewer in which the owner lives were exempt. (policy.txt, line 5)
